intro.header: Equations with Unknowns on Both Sides
intro.objective: Solve linear equations where the unknown appears on both sides. Collect the letter terms on one side and the numbers on the other, then solve the simpler equation.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to do the move to both sides — subtract the same letter term from each side.
Moving the larger letter term, which can leave a negative coefficient unnecessarily.
Sign errors when subtracting a term: 5x − 3x = 2x, not 8x.
Stopping at ax = c and forgetting the final division.
methodSteps: Step 1: Decide which side will keep the letters — usually the side with more of them.
Step 2: Subtract the smaller letter term from both sides.
Step 3: You now have a number on only one side — collect the numbers using inverses.
Step 4: Solve the resulting one- or two-step equation.
Step 5: Check by substituting into the original equation (both sides should match).
workedExample: Step 1 — Keep letters on the left (it has more x).

methodReminder: 1  Choose the side to keep the letters
2  Subtract the smaller letter term (both sides)

frame: Take the smaller letter term away from both sides first.
Move the letters one way and the numbers the other.

questions.content:
Solve. Keep the side that gives a positive letter term.

   a) 3x + 8 = 7x
   b) 2x − 5 = 5x + 4
   c) 10 − x = 4 + x

Sara and Tom have the same number of sweets.
Sara has (4x + 2) sweets and Tom has (6x − 8) sweets.

   a) Form an equation. (1 mark)
   b) Solve it to find x. (1 mark)
   c) How many sweets does each person have? (1 mark)

Two phone plans cost the same for g gigabytes of data.
Plan A: £10 plus £2 per GB.   Plan B: £4 plus £4 per GB.

   a) Form an equation in g. (1 mark)
   b) Solve it to find the number of GB where the plans cost the same. (2 marks)
   c) What is that cost? (1 mark)

Two metal rods are the same length.
Rod A is (5x − 3) cm long and Rod B is (2x + 9) cm long.

   a) Find x. (2 marks)
   b) Find the length of each rod. (1 mark)
   c) A third rod is 5 cm shorter than twice the length of Rod A. Find its length. (2 marks)
